predictions.text: Milwaukee returns home for Game 2 of the World Series holding a 103-59 regular-season record, the best run differential in the majors at plus 214, and a 55-26 home mark. The Brewers have won five straight and eight of their last ten, while Tampa Bay went 43-38 on the road and 5-5 over the same ten-game span. Logan Henderson takes the ball against Drew Rasmussen, and Milwaukee's 832 runs scored are 96 more than Tampa Bay managed across 162 games. The selection is the Brewers moneyline.

Milwaukee's offence is the reason to take the road side in Game 3. The Brewers scored 832 runs across 162 games, 96 more than Tampa Bay, and finished 48-33 away with a plus-214 run differential that was the best in the majors. Robert Gasser is scheduled against Freddy Peralta, and Tampa Bay's 55-26 home record is the counter-argument, but the Rays managed a 5-5 close to the season. At close to even money, the stronger lineup and the deeper season-long margin make Milwaukee the selection on the moneyline.

Ottawa has banked 14 points from eleven games and is 4-2-0 at the Canadian Tire Centre, while the Rangers have collected just one win in six road games despite a perfect 6-0-0 record at home. New York has scored 37 goals and conceded 29, but eight of those goals for came in a single home stand and the road split is 1-4-1. Ottawa's 31 goals for and 30 against suggest a tight game, and home ice plus the sharp travel split points to the Senators. The selection is Ottawa on the moneyline.

Nashville is not the side the standings suggest at first glance: it has conceded 30 goals in nine games, 3.33 per game, while Pittsburgh has shipped 38 in eleven, 3.45 per game, and has lost six of those eleven. The Penguins' 37 goals for flatter a 4-6-1 record, and only three of their wins have come at PPG Paints Arena in six home starts. The Predators are 1-1-2 on the road, so this is a narrow call rather than a confident one, and our fair price of -131 reflects a game that could go either way. The selection is Nashville on the moneyline.

Washington is 4-2-0 at Capital One Arena with a plus-one goal differential, and Buffalo arrives at 1-1-2 on the road having been outscored 37-28 across ten games. The Sabres have lost their last outing and have allowed four or more goals in four of their ten starts. Both clubs have ten points, but the Capitals have done it with a steadier defensive record, conceding 29 goals to Buffalo's 37. Home ice and the shot-suppression edge make Washington the selection on the moneyline.

Carolina is the form team of the early season at 8-2-2 with 18 points, a 6-1-1 road record and an 8-1-1 mark over its last ten. The Hurricanes have scored 47 goals and conceded 33, while St. Louis is 5-4-1 and has been outscored on the road despite a 3-0-1 home record. The Blues have won two straight, but those wins came against sides outside the current top ten, and their 35 goals for is twelve fewer than Carolina's. The selection is Carolina on the moneyline.

Tampa Bay has allowed 29 goals in ten games, 2.90 per game, against Utah's 36 in eleven, and that defensive gap is the basis for backing the road side. The Lightning are 7-3-0 overall but only 2-3-0 away, while Utah is 3-1-0 at the Delta Center and has scored 41 goals, so the risk is real. The counterweight is that Utah has conceded four or more in four of its eleven starts and lost its last game. At a fair price of -113 the Lightning's superior goals-against rate is worth the travel risk. Selection: Tampa Bay moneyline.

Seattle has 15 points from eleven games and has won two straight, scoring 38 goals against 36. Minnesota is 2-3-2 on the road and has dropped its last game, with 32 goals for and 27 against. The Wild's defensive numbers are the better of the two, so this is closer than the raw points suggest, but home ice and Seattle's 3-2-1 record at Climate Pledge Arena edge it. With no official start time captured for this fixture, treat the price as provisional. The selection is Seattle on the moneyline.

predictions.selection: Daniil Medvedev to win the Almaty Open final
predictions.text: Medvedev reached the Almaty final by beating third seed Alexander Bublik 6-3, with Bublik retiring, while Basilashvili needed three sets to see off seventh seed Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4 6-7(5) 6-3. The Georgian has therefore spent considerably more time on court across the semi-finals. No official ranking, head-to-head or serving data was captured for this desk, so no price is offered and the confidence stays low. The selection is Medvedev to win the title.

predictions.selection: Taylor Fritz to win the Lyon final
predictions.text: Fritz came through his semi-final against Tommy Paul 6-3 7-5 without dropping a set, while Musetti had to save four match points before beating top seed Flavio Cobolli 4-6 6-2 7-5. That is a heavy physical and emotional cost to carry into a final 24 hours later. Fritz also holds the higher seeding of the two, at second against sixth. No official ranking or head-to-head page was captured, so no price is published. The selection is Fritz to win the Lyon title.

Charlotte is 1-1 and Miami is 0-2, and the split matters more than the raw records: the Heat have played both games at home and lost both, while the Hornets won their only road game and lost at home. Our numbers make Charlotte a 56 per cent favourite, a thin edge rather than a strong one, so this is a low-confidence call. No official injury report was readable for either roster, which keeps availability an open risk. Selection: Charlotte Hornets to win.

Philadelphia is 2-0 with one home win and one road win, while Milwaukee has opened 0-2 with a defeat in each column. That start is the reason our numbers make the 76ers a 60.5 per cent favourite, the clearest edge on tonight's basketball board. Two games is a small sample, so the edge is treated as medium rather than high confidence. Official injury status could not be read for this fixture. Selection: Philadelphia 76ers to win.

Both teams are 2-0, but the routes differ: Houston won once at home and once away, while Atlanta won both of its games on the road and now plays its home opener. Our numbers give the Hawks a 51.7 per cent edge once home court is applied, which is close to a coin flip and is why this stays low confidence. Two-game samples are thin, and no official injury report was readable. Selection: Atlanta Hawks to win.

Dallas is 1-1 and San Antonio is 0-2, and the Spurs have lost both of their games at home, which is the wrong pattern to carry into a road trip. The Mavericks' win came away from home, and our numbers make them a 56 per cent favourite with home court. That is a modest edge rather than a commanding one, and the official injury report was not readable for this desk. Selection: Dallas Mavericks to win.

Golden State is 0-2 with one home defeat and one road defeat, while Phoenix is 0-1 after losing its only game away from home. Both teams are chasing a first win, but the Suns get home court and our numbers make them a 56 per cent favourite, thin enough to keep the call at low confidence. No official injury report was available for either roster. Selection: Phoenix Suns to win.
